rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir treats the report and the Bedouin's prayer as support for permissibility of invoking mercy on the Prophet, which he says is the majority view.
rows.anchor: فيستدل بهذا الحديث من ذهب إلى جواز الترحم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما هو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qadi Iyad reports that most Malikis prohibit invoking mercy on the Prophet, while Abu Muhammad Ibn Abi Zayd permits it.
rows.anchor: وحكى القاضي عياض عن جمهور المالكية منعه، قال: وأجازه أبو محمد بن أبي زيد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Bedouin asked Allah to show mercy to him and Muhammad alone; the Prophet replied that he had restricted a vast mercy.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عامر بن ربيعة
rows.claim: عامر بن ربيعة reports the Prophet saying that angels continue praying for whoever prays for him, whether the person does so little or much; Ibn Majah also transmits it through Shuʿba.
rows.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عامر بن ربيعة يحدث عن أبيه قال: سمعت النبي

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: Two Ahmad routes from Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf recount the Prophet's long prostration and Gabriel's message that God blesses whoever blesses the Prophet and greets whoever greets him.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتبعته حتى دخل نخلا

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar found the Prophet prostrating; Gabriel conveyed that one prayer from a member of the community earns ten divine prayers and ten degrees. Al-Diya al-Maqdisi selected this report in his Mustakhraj on the Sahihayn.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه، قال: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لحاجة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet saying that those who pray for him most will be nearest to him on the Day of Resurrection; al-Tirmidhi alone transmits it and calls it hasan gharib.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: يعقوب بن زيد بن طلحة
rows.claim: Yaqub ibn Zayd ibn Talha relays a report that praying for the Prophet earns ten divine prayers and that dedicating one's whole prayer to him lets God suffice one's worldly and next-world concerns; Sufyan did not know its transmitter link.
rows.anchor: عن يعقوب بن زيد بن طلحة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb asks how much of his prayer to devote to the Prophet; the versions increase the suggested share from a third to all, with the all-prayer version promising forgiveness or relief from anxieties. Al-Tirmidhi grades his version hasan.
rows.anchor: عن الطفيل بن أبي بن كعب، عن أبيه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخرج في جوف الليل

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ahmad transmits Ubayy's shorter version: a man asks whether making all his prayer for the Prophet will suffice, and is told that God will suffice his worldly and next-world concerns.
rows.anchor: عن الطفيل بن أبي، عن أبيه قال: قال رجل: يا رسول الله، أرأيت إن جعلت صلاتي كلها عليك؟

rows.speaker: أبو طلحة
rows.claim: Abu Talha reports that an angel told the Prophet that God blesses ten times whoever from his community prays for him, and returns tenfold greeting to whoever greets him; the Prophet assented.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء ذات يوم، والسرور يرى في وجهه

rows.speaker: أبو طلحة الأنصاري
rows.claim: In Ahmad's other report, Gabriel says one prayer for the Prophet earns ten good deeds, erases ten sins, raises ten degrees, and is returned in kind; Ibn Kathir calls its chain good, though the canonical collectors omit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي طلحة الأنصاري قال: أصبح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما طيب النفس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that whoever prays for the Prophet once receives ten divine prayers; al-Tirmidhi grades this report hasan sahih, and Muslim, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasaʾi also transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه؛ عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Ahmad's Abu Hurayra report calls prayer for the Prophet a purification for the worshipper and says to ask God for al-wasila, the highest Garden's rank, which the Prophet hopes to receive.
rows.anchor: عن كعب، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar's parallel from Mujahid and Abu Hurayra likewise urges prayer and asking for al-wasila, described as the highest Garden's single rank that the Prophet hopes will be his.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some transmitters criticize the chain of al-Bazzar's preceding report.
rows.anchor: في إسناده بعض من تكلم فيه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr reports that one prayer for the Prophet brings seventy prayers from God and the angels.
rows.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عمرو يقول: من صلى على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: In a separate farewell-like report, the Prophet says he is the unlettered final prophet, has been given comprehensive speech and knowledge of Hell's keepers and Throne-bearers, and tells the community to obey him then follow God's Book.
rows.anchor: وسمعت عبد الله بن عمرو يقول: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما كالمودع

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction that whoever hears his name mentioned should pray for him, and that one prayer earns ten divine prayers.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A second report from Anas says one prayer for the Prophet brings ten divine prayers and removes ten sins.
rows.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسين بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the report that a miser is one who hears the Prophet mentioned but does not pray for him as hasan gharib sahih; transmitters differ whether its Companion source is al-Husayn or Ali.
rows.anchor: ورواه الترمذي من حديث سليمان بن بلال، ثم قال: هذا حديث حسن غريب صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that some transmitters attribute the miser report to al-Husayn ibn Ali, while others make it a report from Ali himself.
rows.anchor: ومن الرواة من جعله من مسند

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports from the Prophet that the most miserly person is one who hears the Prophet mentioned but does not pray for him.
rows.anchor: عن عوف بن مالك، عن أبي ذر، رضي الله عنه؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri gives a mursal version: sufficient miserliness is for a person to be mentioned and not pray for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: حدثنا جرير بن حازم، سمعت الحسن يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports three disgraced people: one who hears the Prophet mentioned without praying for him, one who lets Ramadan pass unforgiven, and one whose aged parents do not admit him to Paradise. Al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan gharib; al-Bukhari and other routes also transmit it, with several other Companions cited.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن أبي سعيد المقبري، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir takes this and the preceding report as evidence that praying for the Prophet is obligatory every time he is mentioned; he attributes this view to a group including al-Tahawi and al-Hulaymi and cites a corroborating Ibn Majah report.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث والذي قبله دليل على وجوب الصلاة عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم كلما ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited for the report that forgetting prayer for the Prophet makes one miss the path to Paradise. Ibn Majah's Jabara route is weak; al-Baqir's mursal version is said to gain support from the earlier report.
rows.anchor: من نسي الصلاة علي خطئ طريق الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view requires one prayer for the Prophet per sitting and recommends it for the rest of that sitting; Ibn Kathir says a report from Abu Hurayra supports this view.
rows.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أنه تجب الصلاة في المجلس مرة واحدة، ثم لا تجب في بقية ذلك المجلس، بل تستحب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that a gathering without remembrance of God or prayer for the Prophet incurs loss and may be punished or forgiven; al-Tirmidhi calls the report hasan.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that people who disperse without praying for the Prophet will regret it, even if they enter Paradise when they see the reward they missed.
rows.anchor: عن ذكوان، عن أبي سعيد قال

rows.speaker: القاضي عياض
rows.claim: Qadi Iyad upholds the view that the verse requires prayer for the Prophet once in a lifetime and recommends more. He reads al-Tabarani's reported consensus for recommendation as applying beyond the obligatory once, comparable to testimony to prophethood.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه إنما تجب الصلاة عليه، عليه السلام، في العمر مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the lifetime-once position strange because prayer for the Prophet is commanded at many times, some obligatory and others recommended.
rows.anchor: قلت: وهذا قول غريب، فإنه قد ورد الأمر بالصلاة عليه في أوقات كثيرة، فمنها واجب، ومنها مستحب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs listeners to answer the caller to prayer, then pray for him and ask God for al-wasila; whoever asks it for him earns his intercession, and the Prophet hopes to receive that Garden rank.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص يقول: أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A second report from Abd Allah ibn Amr says that whoever asks God to grant the Prophet al-wasila is entitled to the Prophet's intercession on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: عن صفوان بن سليم، عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra urges prayer for the Prophet as purification and asking God for al-wasila, the Garden's highest rank reserved for one man whom the Prophet hopes to be.
rows.anchor: عن كعب -هو كعب الأحبار -عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رويفع بن ثابت الأنصاري
rows.claim: Ruwayfiʿ ibn Thabit reports that whoever prays for Muhammad and asks God to place him at the honored station near Him on Judgment Day earns the Prophet's intercession.
rows.anchor: عن رويفع بن ثابت الأنصاري؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ruwayfiʿ's report has an acceptable chain, though the canonical collectors do not include it.
rows.anchor: وهذا إسناد لا بأس به، ولم يخرجوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas offers a supplication asking God to accept Muhammad's great intercession, raise his rank, grant his requests in both lives, and give him as He gave Abraham and Moses; Ibn Kathir calls its chain good, strong, and sound.
rows.anchor: سمعت ابن عباس يقول: اللهم تقبل شفاعة محمد الكبرى، وارفع درجته العليا

rows.speaker: فاطمة بنت رسول الله
rows.claim: Fatima reports that the Prophet prayed for himself when entering and leaving the mosque, then asked forgiveness and for the gates of mercy on entry and bounty on exit to be opened.
rows.anchor: عن جدته [فاطمة] (12) بنت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talib said that when passing mosques people should pray for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين قال: قال علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that scholars including al-Shafiʿi require prayer for the Prophet in the final tashahhud.
rows.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى ذلك من العلماء مع (3) الشافعي، رحمه الله

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The first tashahhud is unanimously not obligatory; whether prayer for the Prophet is recommended there is disputed in two Shafiʿi positions.
rows.anchor: وأما التشهد الأول فلا تجب فيه قولا واحدا، وهل تستحب؟ على قولين للشافعي

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل
rows.claim: The funeral-prayer practice is to recite al-Fatiha after the first takbir, pray for the Prophet after the second, supplicate for the deceased after the third, and make a closing supplication after the fourth.
rows.anchor: أن السنة في الصلاة على الجنازة أن يكبر الإمام، ثم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب بعد التكبيرة الأولى سرا

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل
rows.claim: Al-Nasaʾi gives Abu Umama's wording that this funeral-prayer order is Sunna; Ibn Kathir says a Companion's statement here counts as marfuʿ according to the sound view. A route via Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and similar reports from Abu Hurayra, Ibn Umar, and al-Shaʿbi are also noted.
rows.anchor: ورواه النسائي، عن أبي أمامة نفسه أنه قال: من السنة، فذكره

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud describes the Eid prayer's sequence: each cycle opens with takbir, praise, prayer for the Prophet, and supplication; after the first cycle's recitation and bowing, the second repeats the praise, prayer, supplication, and takbirs. Hudhayfa and Abu Musa affirm him; the chain is sahih.
rows.anchor: أن ابن مسعود وأبا موسى وحذيفة خرج عليهم الوليد بن عقبة يوما قبل العيد

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar is quoted by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib as saying supplication remains suspended between heaven and earth until one prays for the Prophet; another route also preserves it as Umar's own statement.
rows.anchor: عن أبي قرة الأسدي، عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Other transmissions raise the suspended-supplication report to the Prophet and add: pray for him at the beginning, middle, and end of supplication, and do not treat him like a rider's waterskin.
rows.anchor: ورواه معاذ بن الحارث، عن أبي قرة، عن سعيد بن المسيب، عن عمر مرفوعا
